problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t\ge 0$ is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-\frac{\pi }{3}).$ At time $t=\frac{\pi }{3}$ the particle is located at the position $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=\pi ?$
worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=\pi $ is equal to its position at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [\frac{\pi }{3},\pi ].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(\pi )=x(\frac{\pi }{3})+{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi }v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Carrying out the computations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{2}+{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-\frac{\pi }{3})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t-\frac{\pi }{3})]}_{\pi /3}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+([-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi -\frac{\pi }{3})]-[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{3})]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+(-(-\frac{1}{2})+1) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=\pi $ is $x=2.$
